taxAdjustments.section: Table D, Tax Recapture (codes F, C and B)
taxAdjustments.note: Dollars added to the bracket tax to take back the benefit of the lower brackets. Shape for single: three stacked ramps, each per $5,000 or part: $25 over $105,000 (10 steps, $250), then $90 over $200,000 (30 steps, $2,950 total), then $50 over $500,000 (9 steps), reaching $3,400 above $540,000. Joint doubles every threshold, width and amount ($6,800 above $1,080,000). Head of household uses thresholds of $168,000, $320,000 and $800,000, $8,000 widths and $40, $140 and $80 steps ($5,320 above $864,000). Points are the rows of the 2026 table, each row's lower bound with its value, since the rows read 'more than X, less than or equal to Y'. The 2025 CT-1040 instructions table is identical row for row. The lookup is on Connecticut AGI (annualized salary in the withholding rules), not taxable income. The DRS tax tables stop at $102,000, so there is no printed tax figure to check this table against.

taxAdjustments.section: Table E, Personal Tax Credits (codes F, C and B)

Points are the rows of the 2026 table, each row's lower bound with its value, since the rows read 'more than X, less than or equal to Y'. The 2025 CT-1040 instructions table is identical row for row. personalExemption.note: This is Utah's taxpayer tax credit before its phase-out, computed rather than read from a table. Filer amounts are 6% of the 2026 federal standard deduction ($16,100 / $32,200 / $24,150), per 59-10-1018(2). Tax Foundation shows the same $966 and $1,932. The dependent amount is 6% of the Utah personal exemption of $2,111, which is the 2025 figure from the TC-40 instructions. The 2026 exemption is indexed and was not published as of November 2026, so only the dependent amount is a 2025 value. The credit is nonrefundable. Filers who itemize use 6% of itemized deductions less state income tax instead. Phase-out rule (59-10-1018(4), TC-40 lines 17 to 19): the total credit is reduced by 1.3 cents for each dollar of Utah taxable income over a base amount, never below zero. The base amounts used are the 2025 ones from the TC-40 instructions ($18,213 single, $36,426 joint, $27,320 head of household). The 2026 base amounts are indexed and were not published as of November 2026. The reduction has no upper limit, so each phaseOut list is two points on the line: the base amount with 0, and the base amount plus $1,000,000 with $13,000.
